title: Restriction commutes with negation
statement: Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \bbf_2$ be a Boolean function and $\rho$ a restriction on $n$ variables. Then restricting the negation of $f$ agrees, at every point $x$, with the negation of the restriction of $f$; that is, $(\lnot f)$ restricted by $\rho$ equals the pointwise negation of $f$ restricted by $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
ρ is a restriction on n variables
